entities.summary:
Bonifatius (b. 350 CE, Thrace) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Thrace.


 He served as the magister militum of the Eastern Roman Empire and played a crucial role in maintaining the empire's borders against the Goths and other barbarian groups.


 Bonifatius' military campaigns and administrative skills were instrumental in securing the empire's eastern provinces and ensuring the continued prosperity of the Roman Empire.


 His legacy as a skilled military leader and administrator has endured for centuries, serving as a model for future generations of Roman officials.


 The inscription on his tombstone, 'Bonifatius, son of Aemilianus, magister militum', stands as a testament to his remarkable achievements and the esteem in which he was held by his contemporaries.
